title: Software engineer, first game: a procedural SAO-style floor built with Claude Code, from the starting city to the tower
author: javon27
selftext:
Got into software dev because of video games. Tried to dabble in it for years, but never had the time (or energy) to get anything going - that and a lack of a good idea. After watching Sword Art Online (SAO) years ago, I started to crave a game that fully captured that feeling of being in Aincrad. I tried FFO, GW2, etc. but nothing gave me that feeling. Then recently Echoes of Aincrad went on sale and I bought it. It finally gave me some of that feeling I was looking for, but also still lacking a lot.

That's when I realized that maybe I can make a better game with AI. A procedurally generated world at the scale of Aincrad in the anime. With NPCs and 10,000 virtual players with fully simulated lives. A game that continues to progress even after you log off. Is it possible? I sure hope so.

I'm building this as a series of small throwaway experiments with Claude Code, each answering one question: can a 10 km floor feel worth exploring, can a city look architected rather than random, can towns read as distinct places, and so on. The generators are headless Python, and a small Godot viewer lets me walk and fly around what they produce.

This clip is floor 1: a flyover, then a run from the starting city's plaza out to the tower that leads up to floor 2. Terrain, rivers, towns, farms, a port, roads and the tower's location all come from one seed.

Longer version (2:38): [https://youtu.be/eOOgKwqmmOc](https://youtu.be/eOOgKwqmmOc)

Experiment logs: [https://jaysontrades.com/devlog/](https://jaysontrades.com/devlog/)

comments.author: Chocoweb88
comments.body:
I think it is great to be ambitious and adventurous, at the same time needs to be realistic and set good expectations.The idea of creating an entire SAO game world with mmorpg elements (plus a world that keep progressing even with a player is offline) sounds really massive for 1 person to build (at least not for me, dont think I will ever have the time and skills to make something that ambitious) so in the end its up to OP to tackle and decide the future of this project.

Personally, I know of SAO and watch a few episodes, but I am not a big fan of mmorpg, and I am not experienced in 3d game design, so I cant say much on OP's early draft (my first impression is that it looks impressive, but not my type of game) And correct me if Im wrong: I think for SAO, the most important and attractive aspect should be the cool and flashy combat, maybe that can be the main scope to start work on, or at least alongside the world building. But then again im not too familiar with SAO, so ignore me if that is not the game experience you are going for. Good luck with your game!

replies.author: javon27
replies.body:
Each of these aspects have been done to some degree. The problem is, there's no one game that puts them all together in the package I've been looking for. Also, with my current workflow, I have Claude spend at least an hour researching each topic, pulling YouTube transcripts (or transcribing them itself), papers on the subject, etc. Then it fact checks what it found before then applying its learnings for me to playtest.

I already simulated an economy, NPC daily lives, generating the map, the towns, etc. A lot of that just in less than a week. I already know it will take months if not years for me to realize my full vision, and I'm all in for it.
